title: CA2 LoRA training infrastructure — tiny smoke through the budget guard (Wave Q — Model Discovery, PR-63)
whatThisIs: A path proof: a real dataset built from admitted PDMX works by CA2's own encoder, a real LoRA fine-tune of the pinned CA2 checkpoint on a tiny overfit subset, a checkpoint written and resumed from, and every gate (rights proof, checksum, budget guard) exercised for real. It is NOT a pilot: no musical claim is made, no tournament was run on the result, and the loss decrease shown is memorisation of 32 examples, which is exactly what the owner's 'tiny overfit test' gate asks for.

manifest.splitRule: work-level: int(sha256(workId).hex[:8], 16) % 100 -> <90 train, <95 val, else test

dedupe.method: sha256 of file bytes + CA2 dedupe_and_filter_midi_files_functions onset-chromagram string over 12 transpositions (sha256 each); CA2's in-file near-equal track removal (_equality_measure, threshold 0.9) runs inside the loader

builder.taskShape: one target track x N consecutive measures masked (tournament shape); mask order ascending by measure, extra_id from 0

tests: python unittest 50 (guard/collator/manifest/split/trainer gates/wall-time ledger/eval hooks/Modal shape), and the same 50 re-run inside the Modal image at build time; TS: trainingManifest 7, trainingBudgetGuard 7; tsc -p artifacts/api-server --noEmit green
runNotes: Two launches, no hand-held state: phase 1 ran steps 1-100 and stopped on request after writing checkpoint step-100; phase 2 resumed from that directory and ran to 200. The wall-time ledger (783.2 s + 684.1 s = 1467.3 s) came out of the checkpoint, not off the command line.

Earlier launches of the same dataset were made while the trainer was still being fixed (a relative --resume was resolved inside the vendored CA2 tree, because importing it chdirs; wall time restarted at zero on resume; a checkpoint did not list itself). Those runs were discarded and the whole smoke was re-run from step 0 with the shipped code, so every number here was produced by the committed trainer.

export_checkpoint.py was run for real on checkpoints/step-200 in both modes. The merged directory reloads as a plain T5ForConditionalGeneration (forward loss 0.146109 on two val rows; generate() returns 52 tokens over the 1944-token vocabulary), which is what a second worker endpoint would serve. No endpoint was deployed and no tournament was run.

The Modal app was deployed and preflighted on the committed sources: the image rebuilt from the release zip (sha checked), ran all 50 unit tests inside the container, and verified the pinned checkpoint at /app/vendor. modalPreflight.imageEvidence below equals modal_train_config.image_evidence() over the committed files, so the container that passed those tests is the one these sources describe. No GPU function was invoked.
honestLimits: CPU only, 32 training examples, 4-measure windows capped at 512 input tokens: a proof that the path works, not a measurement of anything musical.
The Modal GPU function was deployed and preflighted (image built, checkpoint verified inside it, volume reachable) but no GPU training run was launched: the one permitted smoke ran locally at $0.
The loss decrease is memorisation of the overfit subset; the held-out curve on 14 never-trained examples is recorded so nobody mistakes the former for generalisation.
The tournament has not been run on any checkpoint from this run; benchmarkResult is null by design until a checkpoint is exported, served on a second endpoint and judged.
